questions.q: At which OSI layer does a switch operate, and what does it use to make forwarding decisions?
options: Layer 1 (Physical), using signal strength
Layer 2 (Data Link), using MAC addresses
Layer 3 (Network), using IP addresses
Layer 4 (Transport), using port numbers
questions.explain: A switch operates at the Data Link layer (OSI layer 2) and forwards frames based on MAC addresses, not IP addresses.

questions.q: How does a switch learn which device is reachable on which port?
options: An administrator must manually type in every MAC address and port
It watches incoming traffic and records which MAC address showed up on which port in a MAC address table
It broadcasts a request to the manufacturer for a device list
It cannot learn this; every frame is always sent out every port
questions.explain: A switch learns dynamically by observing frames as they arrive, building a MAC address table that maps addresses to ports, so future frames go directly to the right port.

questions.q: What does a router use to decide where to forward a packet, and what does it consult to do so?
options: MAC addresses, consulting a MAC address table
IP addresses, consulting a routing table of known destination networks
Port numbers, consulting a firewall rule list
Device names, consulting a DNS server
questions.explain: A router operates at the Network layer and forwards packets based on IP addresses, using a routing table that lists known destination networks and how to reach each one.

questions.q: When a laptop on Northbridge's corporate office subnet needs to reach a destination that isn't on its own subnet, where does it first send the packet?
options: Directly to the destination device, skipping any intermediate device
To its default gateway, which is the router
To the nearest switch's MAC address table
It broadcasts the packet to every device on the subnet
questions.explain: When the destination isn't on the device's own subnet, the device sends the packet to its default gateway — the router — which then decides where to forward it next.

questions.q: What is a router's default route used for?
options: It is the first route checked before any other entry in the routing table
It is the fallback path used when no more specific route in the routing table matches the destination
It only applies to traffic between two switches
It disables all other routes until manually re-enabled
questions.explain: A default route is the fallback a router uses for destinations that don't match any more specific entry in its routing table — typically the path out toward the internet.
